chunks: Abul Faḍl Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Sulaymān narrated to me from Mūsā ibn Muḥammad ibn Mūsā, from Muḥammad ibn Muḥammad Al-Ash’ath, who said: Abil Ḥasan Mūsā ibn Ismā’īl ibn Mūsā ibn Ja’far narrated to me, from his father, from his grandfather, Ja’far ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from ‘Ali ibn Ḥusayn (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allāh (peace be upon him and his family) said: Whoever visits my grave after my death is like one who immigrated to me during my life. So if you cannot [come], send me salām, for verily it reaches me.
ai.seo_question: What is the reward for visiting the Prophet's grave and what if one cannot go in person?
ai.summary: This hadith from Kamil al-Ziyarat underscores the enduring spiritual presence of the Prophet (s) in Shia theology, equating posthumous visitation with the high merit of Hijrah. It highlights the practical flexibility of devotion by affirming that sending salām suffices for those unable to travel, reinforcing the concept of the Prophet's awareness of his community's greetings across time.
